data.text: The evidence is consistent. Let me confirm the timeline once more from state.json before acting.
I have enough to conclude. The timeline from the watchdog records and current state is consistent:

data.reason: Modem lost upstream sync at 02:01:44 (T3 timeout), failed re-registration (TFTP config NOT FOUND) at 02:14, and only completed re-registration at 02:28:21 (now OPERATIONAL). The firewall's vtnet0 still holds the pre-outage DHCP lease (fixed-address 198.51.100.27 via server 203.0.113.67) and cannot reach the ISP gateway (ping 198.51.100.1 = 100% loss) though L2/ARP to the CPE works. A WAN reload to renew the DHCP lease against the now-re-registered link is the appropriate recovery; the watchdog is in observe mode so it only logged 'would_reload'.

data.error: action must be one of: change_config, contact_provider, investigate_further, none, reboot_host, replace_hardware, restart_service

data.component: WAN interface (vtnet0) DHCP lease / ISP link
data.cause: The ISP link dropped at ~02:01 when the cable modem lost upstream synchronization (T3 timeout) and failed re-registration (TFTP config file NOT FOUND), only completing re-registration at 02:28; the firewall's WAN interface kept its stale pre-outage DHCP lease and never recovered connectivity, so the internet stayed down even after the modem became OPERATIONAL.
evidence: Modem log shows 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 02:01:44 and 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND' at 02:14:10, matching the outage start (~02:01): cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl

Modem reached 'registration complete' only at 02:28:21, and metrics show cm_status NOT_SYNCHRONIZED at 02:06 becoming OPERATIONAL from 02:29 with heavy correctable errors (corrected 52070, uncorrected 131): cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl and modem-metrics.jsonl

Watchdog logged outage_start at 02:06 and 'would_reload' decisions at 02:30 and 02:40 (reason: modem_operational, then retry) because it runs in observe mode and cannot act; state.json shows reloads_in_outage=2, last_action=reload: cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl and state.json

Firewall still routes via default gateway 198.51.100.1 on vtnet0 with address 198.51.100.27, but ping to 198.51.100.1 shows 100% packet loss while ARP has an entry for it — L2 to the CPE exists, no end-to-end path: netstat -rn, ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1, arp -a

DHCP lease on file is a long-lived one (lease-time 172800, renew 2026/3/5) from server 203.0.113.67, i.e. unchanged through the outage, so the WAN was never renegotiated after the modem re-registered: cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0
LAN side is healthy — ping to LAN host 10.20.0.9 succeeds with 0% loss, consistent with 'local services still work': ping -c 3 -n 10.20.0.9
data.recommendation: Reload/renew the WAN interface's DHCP lease (wan_reload, already requested and executed in this drill) now that the modem has re-registered and reports OPERATIONAL, so vtnet0 renegotiates addressing with the ISP and connectivity is restored. If outages like this recur, consider letting the watchdog act automatically once the modem settles as operational instead of only observing, and ask the ISP about the TFTP 'configuration file NOT FOUND' errors during the modem's re-registration attempts.
